title: Uniform cohomological bounds in the finite-type range
statement:
Let $k$ be a finite or algebraically closed field, let $X,Y$ be schemes of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $g:X\to Y$ be a morphism of finite type. Use small sites in a common larger universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For a finite-type $k$-scheme $T$ put $d_T=\dim T$ if $T\ne\varnothing$ and $d_T=0$ if $T=\varnothing$, and put $e_T=2d_T+1$; dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $G$ be a torsion abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$, where torsion means every local section is locally killed by a positive integer [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], without a uniform annihilator. Write $\nu_T:T_{\Proet}\to T_{\Et}$ for comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Restrictions along a scheme map mean the corresponding inverse images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Cohomology means right-derived global sections [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology].

1. If $U=\varprojlim_iU_i$ is a pro-étale affine presentation over $X$ [sk-def-pe-morphisms], with $U$ an object of $X_{\Proet}$ and $U_i$ affine étale over $X$, then $H^q(U_{\Proet},(\nu_X^*G)|_U)=0$ for $q>e_X$.
2. If $V=\varprojlim_iV_i$ is such a presentation over $Y$, with $V$ an object of $Y_{\Proet}$ and $V_i$ affine étale over $Y$, then, writing $T=X\times_YV$ for the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product],
$$H^q(T_{\Proet},(\nu_X^*G)|_T)=0\qquad(q>e_X).$$
3. The higher direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] satisfies $R^qg_{\Et,*}G=0$ for $q>e_X$.

Each presentation has a small nonempty cofiltered index category and affine transition maps. The same assertions apply with $Y$ as source, a torsion sheaf on $Y_{\Et}$, and bound $e_Y$ (and any finite-type map from $Y$ to a finite-type $k$-scheme).

proof.text: For finite k apply lem-sfb-finite-field-all-torsion-cd. For algebraically closed k, use the separably closed bound zero and monotonicity to obtain the all-torsion bound one.

Use finite_dimension_bound to identify the canonical natural dimension bound, including the empty scheme. The source-library finite-type torsion bound, with field bound one, gives 2*d+1. Affine etale stages have finite-type structure over k. Their dimensions are at most the source dimension: an etale morphism has discrete fibres, so its continuous map identifies no distinct specializing points and maps each strict chain to a strict chain. This is implemented by the proved source theorem Scheme.Hom.topologicalKrullDim_le_of_etale.

For a pro-affine-etale presentation, unpack its cofiltered affine etale diagram. Maps between its affine stages are affine. Apply the affine-limit cohomological-dimension theorem to the common stage bound.

For the product, lift the presentation to Over Y. The right adjoint Over.pullback g and the connected-limit-preserving forgetful functor carry its limiting cone to a limiting cone of fibre products. Pullback pasting identifies each transition as the base change of an affine transition. The stages are finite type over k using their map to the affine stage over Y, hence qcqs, and etale over X, hence bounded by dim X. Apply the affine-limit theorem and transport the cone vertex through pullback symmetry. No k-compatibility of g is used.

For each of the two absolute bounds, pullback preserves torsion. The source comparisonUpperStarCompUpperStarIso identifies the actual coefficient with the comparison of the etale inverse image. Convert total derived sections to classical right derived sections by homologyRightDerivedFunctorObjSingleFunctorIso and the terminal-object global-sections isomorphism. Apply the source abelian comparison theorem isZero_rightDerived_globalSectionsFunctor_comparisonUpperStar_obj and transport back.

Apply lem-sfb-higher-direct-image-affine-etale-bound to the stage bounds to obtain clause 3. Assemble the three clauses. Repeat the same uniform_bounds_of_field_cd proof for source Y and arbitrary target Z. All arguments include empty schemes through dimension bot_le and the supplied all-torsion bounds.

proof_origin.place: Steps 1--11, implemented with source-library abelian comparison, finite-type torsion bounds, Over.pullback on limiting cones, and the two proved helper theorems; U5, 2026-10-19

split_report.route_note: Unit step 1 says "Since X and Y are separated over k", although its statement and this detail assume only finite type. For example the affine line with doubled origin, glued from two copies of A^1_k on D(t), is of finite type over k and is not separated: the diagonal closure contains the pair of distinct origins. The separated-Cech sentence cannot be used under the stated hypotheses. The present split realizes the same step 1 uniform bounds by the all-torsion absolute-bound/affine-limit/comparison argument explicitly supplied by this detail’s own main-20261015 proof; no unit or chapter statement is changed.
